category_title: Students accustomed to strict, non-negotiable disciplinary models
minimal_context: The student is given multiple worksheets to complete during regular classroom instruction.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Here are three more worksheets for you to complete before the end of class.

STUDENT: You only give us a lot of work.

TUTOR: Please just focus on finishing the assignment.

STUDENT: Are you going to grade them this time? You never even grade them.

TUTOR: These are just for practice, they won't be graded. Keep working.

STUDENT: Then there are some teachers who are always angry. And they only give us a lot of work and they never even grade them. You just don't accept me.

options.A: Maintain a consistent ratio of praise to correction at 3:1 or 4:1 during regular classroom instruction.
options.B: Adapt the interactional style when dealing with this student rather than dealing with them in the same way as mainstream students.
options.C: Provide extra time to complete the assigned worksheets by offering flexibility with the overall assignment timelines.
options.D: Offer the choice of a preferred activity contingent upon the student meeting a daily worksheet completion goal.
